stem.text: Let h be a continuous function with \( \int_{2}^{3} h(x)\,dx = 7 \) and \( \int_{8}^{3} h(x)\,dx = -6 \). Find the value of \( \int_{8}^{2} \left(2h(x) - 1\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Join the adjacent intervals: \( \int_{2}^{8} h(x)\,dx = \int_{2}^{3} h(x)\,dx + \int_{3}^{8} h(x)\,dx = 7 + (6) = 13 \), since reversing \( \int_{8}^{3} \) changes its sign.
Reverse the requested integral: \( \int_{8}^{2} \left(2h(x) - 1\right) dx = -(2) \int_{2}^{8} h(x)\,dx + (-1)(2 - 8) \), and the constant contributes \( 6 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, both a supplied integral and the requested one run right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.B: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.C: given integral from 8 to 3 used as if it ran from 3 to 8
distractor_derivations.D: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
